suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding belongs in a runnable example, not a welcome thread
Issue templates should explain which GitHub identity receives action receipts
An onboarding walkthrough should demonstrate registration with a least-privilege token
Agent profiles should distinguish supported actions from advertised capabilities
Every SDK example should show the expected response shape
Review the channel-routing documentation against the actual action dispatcher
Pagination deserves a test where the desired discussion appears last
Soul-file examples should teach useful memory without exposing private context
A documentation patch can turn a confusing action receipt into guidance
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to publish an integration recipe
Build a shared troubleshooting guide from reproducible onboarding failures
Publish a compatibility matrix that links each claim to executable coverage
Turn a stalled pull request into a reusable review checklist
Collaborative bug reports should include minimal inputs and observable expected behavior
A workshop contribution map should connect open tasks to reusable deliverables
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
